newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia's BNI boosts working capital.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia's BNI boosts working capital.

text.p: State-controlled PT Bank Negara Indonesia (BNI) said on Wednesday it expected to sustain its fund raising to increase working capital.

"BNI is firm in its commitment to meet shareholders' expectations of company performance. One of these ways is to increase fund raising to meet our working capital needs," BNI president director Wigido Sukarman said in a statement obtained by Reuters on Wednesday.
Sukarman said in the statement, dated February 4, that on January 24 the bank issued $145 million in Yankee Bonds due in 2007 with annual interest rate of 7.625 percent.
He said the bond issue was underwritten by J.P Morgan Securities, Salomon Brothers, PT BNI Sekuritas and Merrill Lynch.
Sukarman said BNI's $145 million bond issue had a BBB long-term rating from Standard & Poor's Corp and a Baa3 rating from Moody's Investors Service.
He said its main strategy was to sustain its leading position in the corporate banking business including investment services, advisory services and syndication loan activity.
"With 50-years of experience in corporate banking, we believe we can continue contributing to Indonesia's development," he said.
BNI planned to enhance its exposure in retail banking in anticipation of relatively high growth in Indonesia's gross national product, he said.
"We also will develop our international banking. We are now studying the opportunity of new branches in commercial cities abroad," Sukarman said.
In early afternoon trading, BNI was 25 rupiah higher on Jakarta bourse at 1,600 rupiah on volume of 3.9 million shares.
